I've been working this land around Quzhou my whole life. Forty-five years. I know what the soil wants and what it will give back. My back isn't what it was, and two of my sons work in the city now, so I can't be as labor-heavy as I used to be. That shapes what I do.

My 18 mu splits naturally in my head. Cotton is our main cash crop — that's the system here. I keep 8 mu in cotton. The other 10 mu I do wheat in winter, then turn it straight to maize after June harvest. That rotation works. It always has.

**Cotton (8 mu):** I've used Bt cotton for years. It saves me spraying against bollworm — that alone is worth it at my age. I still spray for aphids and spider mites though, can't avoid that. Cotton drinks a lot of fertilizer, especially potassium, and it needs water at budding and boll-setting stages. I'll irrigate 4 times from my well. I plough deep before transplanting — cotton roots go down far.

**Wheat (10 mu):** I plant in mid-October. I use an improved variety the seed shop here sells — not traditional seed anymore, yields are better. I always do the winter water right after sowing, then water again at jointing and heading stage, maybe one more at grain fill if it's dry. Four waterings. I'll plough and prep the bed properly.

**Maize (10 mu, same land as wheat):** Right after wheat comes off in June, I get the maize seed in fast. I use hybrid — everyone around here does, the yield difference is obvious. June-July usually gets some rain so I might only need to irrigate twice. I don't plow again — just rotary till to save time and get the seed in quick.
